correctness.rationale: The final, narrowed infinite-dimensional claim is reconstructed from exact orthogonal projections: v has unit norm, P1 and P2 are orthogonal and P3 nonzero, giving bounded self-adjoint A=-P2-2P3 with precisely {0,-1,-2} and simple positive leading v. Matrix coefficients outside antisymmetric pairs are (1-e^-2t)v_i v_j>0; paired coefficients are (1-e^-2t)(c_k^2-1/[2(1+e^t)]). At each fixed t>0, k large makes this negative, while for fixed k it is eventually positive; diagonals are positive and ||e^{tA}-P1||=e^-t. Exact rational spectral and threshold checks corroborate but do not replace the proof. It does NOT imply every positive initial vector has an eventually positive orbit.
